Name: Felix
Summary: Felix was the Roman governor who kept Paul in custody at Caesarea for two years, hearing him often and hoping for a bribe, and who trembled at Paul's preaching on righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, yet left Paul bound to please the Jews.
KeyStory: Felix heard Paul often, trembled at judgment to come, and left him bound when a successor came.
LifeLesson: Felix trembled and postponed, and postponement became his verdict. A convenient season never came.
